definitions.explanation: The act of separating or saying goodbye; a departure from someone or something.

examples.japanese: {友人|ゆうじん}との{別|わか}れは{辛|つら}かった。
examples.english: Parting with my friend was painful.

examples.japanese: {別|わか}れの{挨拶|あいさつ}をした。
{出会|であ}いがあれば{別|わか}れもある。
examples.english: Where there are meetings, there are also partings.
examples.notes: A common saying about the nature of relationships

examples.japanese: {空港|くうこう}での{別|わか}れは{何度|なんど}{経験|けいけん}しても{慣|な}れない。
examples.english: No matter how many times I experience it, I can never get used to saying goodbye at the airport.

examples.japanese: {卒業式|そつぎょうしき}の{日|ひ}、{先生|せんせい}と{生徒|せいと}たちは{涙|なみだ}の{別|わか}れを{惜|お}しんだ。
examples.english: On graduation day, the teacher and students shed tears, reluctant to part.
examples.notes: {別|わか}れを{惜|お}しむ = to be reluctant to part

notes:
USAGE: {別|わか}れ is the noun form of the verb {別|わか}れる (to part, to separate). It often carries emotional weight, suggesting sadness or significance.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{別|わか}れを{告|つ}げる (to bid farewell)
・{別|わか}れの{言葉|ことば} (parting words)
・{別|わか}れの{挨拶|あいさつ} (farewell greeting)
・{別|わか}れを{惜|お}しむ (to be reluctant to part)
・{永遠|えいえん}の{別|わか}れ (eternal parting, death)
